# How Advertisers can Connect CTV Spend to Business Outcomes with Viant’s New CAPI Performance Report


November 18, 2026 in[Blog](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/)


## Key Takeaways


- **Connect the conversion data you already own:** Send online and offline conversion events from your own systems directly to Viant through Conversion API (CAPI), a secure server-to-server connection.
- **See how campaigns perform against first-party outcomes:** Viant’s new CAPI Performance Report shows attributed conversions for named events such as purchases and RFI submissions.
- **Connect Outcomes Across[CTV](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/omnichannel/connected-tv/) and the Open Internet:** Connect advertiser-owned conversion data to campaigns across CTV and the open internet, including outcomes that happen later, on another device or in a store.
- **Guide What You Do Next:** Use those outcome-based insights to understand what is driving results and inform future decisions about audiences, channels, creative and budget.


---


The customer journey rarely happens in one browser session. People might see an ad while streaming their favorite TV show, research the brand on their phone, and later complete the purchase online or in a store. The advertiser can see that purchase event in its own systems, but connecting it back to the campaign or exposure that influenced it can be difficult, particularly when teams rely on last-touch attribution or evaluate brand and performance activity in separate silos.


That leaves demand-generation channels like[CTV](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/omnichannel/connected-tv/) judged only on the fraction of the customer journey they can track. This is a measurement gap, not a limit on the value that channels like CTV can deliver. CTV can create demand and drive measurable business outcomes, but the prevailing challenge for advertisers is connecting those outcomes back to the exposure.


Viant’s Conversion API (CAPI) is a secure server-to-server connection that sends an advertiser’s own first-party conversion data, including online and offline outcomes, directly to the Viant advertising platform. Viant’s new CAPI Performance Report shows how campaigns perform against that data, giving advertisers a way to connect first-party outcomes to CTV measurement and optimization.


## What is First-Party Conversion Data?


First-party conversion data is information an advertiser collects directly through its own business systems. It can include purchases, qualified leads, subscriptions, bookings, store activity, revenue, and other outcomes that show what happened after a customer interacted with a brand.


This data is valuable because it reflects the advertiser’s own definition of a meaningful result. A retailer may care about an in-store purchase. A[travel](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/travel-tourism/) company may care about a completed booking. An[auto](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/auto/) brand may care about a qualified lead or dealership visit. A[CPG](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/cpg/) advertiser may care about sales tied to a specific product or category.


When those outcomes are connected to media data, advertisers can move beyond reporting metrics like impressions and better understand which exposures contributed to conversions, which creative assets are driving valuable outcomes, and ultimately, where should the next dollar be invested.


## How does CAPI connect first-party data to Viant?


With CAPI, advertisers can send those selected conversion events from its own systems directly to Viant.


Viant offers multiple ways to connect first-party data, including a direct API and integrations with Tealium, Amperity, Freshpaint, Hightouch and Ours Privacy. Viant provides credentials, documentation, example payloads, and onboarding support to help teams authenticate and map their conversion data to the required format. Most advertisers can complete integration after a minimum of two weeks. Once connected, the data flows automatically without recurring manual uploads.


The process works in four steps:


1. An advertiser’s campaign reaches a household through CTV or another channel.
2. The advertiser records a conversion in its own systems, whether the outcome happens online, offline, on another device or later in the customer journey.
3. CAPI sends the relevant conversion event to Viant through a secure server-to-server connection.
4. Viant makes the conversion data available for campaign reporting and, where enabled, optimization against the outcomes the advertiser has defined.


## What can advertisers see in the CAPI Performance Report?


Viant’s CAPI Performance Report is a dedicated Advanced Report in the free report suite. It shows how campaigns perform against the conversion data an advertiser sends through CAPI.


Advertisers can see their own named conversion events, such as purchases or RFI submissions, alongside attributed conversions. Sending additional fields, such as a category, product or store ID, can unlock more detailed breakdowns and help advertisers understand where performance is coming from.


It also gives teams a more useful way to explain CTV performance internally, particularly when conversions happen outside the browser or after the initial ad exposure.


## How can richer signals improve CTV campaigns?


Industry research points to the value advertisers place on these connections.[In an October 2025 survey conducted by IAB](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/IAB_The_Role_of_ConversionAPI_in_Closing_the_Outcome_Gap_for_CTV_October_2025.pdf) , two-thirds of participating advertisers and agencies reported improved ROAS after implementing Conversion APIs. The survey also found that advertisers use CAPI signals for audience targeting and suppression, bid-strategy adjustments and budget reallocation based on conversion performance.


With richer conversion signals, advertisers can work toward:


- **More complete measurement:** See named events from the advertiser’s own systems, including outcomes browser-based tracking may miss.
- **Faster learning cycles:** Create a more direct connection between campaign exposure, conversion data and optimization decisions.
- **More informed allocation:** Understand which audiences, publishers, and creative are contributing to valuable outcomes.
- **Greater confidence in CTV:** Evaluate CTV based on business results, not only impressions, reach, or last-click activity.


CAPI allows advertisers to connect the dots between conversions and campaigns, moving beyond optimizing CTV with typical metrics like impressions, reach, frequency, and video completion rate.


## Which Advertisers Should Use CAPI?


CAPI is especially relevant for advertisers whose customer journeys extend beyond a browser session or whose conversion value lives in offline systems.[Retail](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/retail/) ,[CPG](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/cpg/) ,[QSR](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/qsr/) ,[travel](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/travel-tourism/) and[auto](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/industry/auto/) advertisers are natural fits, but any advertiser with meaningful conversion data in its own systems can benefit from connecting those outcomes to its media strategy.


The right conversion events depend on the business. A retailer might send purchases and store IDs, while a travel advertiser might send bookings and booking value. Sending the outcomes closest to business value gives campaigns and reporting a more useful signal to work with.


## Ready to See It In Action?


Connect your conversion data and start using the CAPI Performance Report today.


To learn more, advertisers can[review Viant’s CAPI integration documentation](https://docs.api.viantinc.com/reference/how-to-get-started) or reach out to their Viant account representative about accessing the CAPI Performance Report.

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a cookieless DSP?Expand


A cookieless DSP is a programmatic advertising platform that identifies and reaches audiences using durable, privacy-first identifiers rather than third-party cookies.


Instead of relying on fragile browser tracking, these platforms leverage advanced solutions like Household ID™ to maintain scale and precision. This approach ensures that digital campaigns remain effective and measurable regardless of evolving browser restrictions or privacy regulations.


How does programmatic advertising work without cookies?Expand


Programmatic advertising functions without cookies by activating first-party data through identity resolution frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 and the Household ID. Marketers also utilize contextual targeting to align ads with real-time content and prioritize natively cookieless channels such as CTV and DOOH. These methods allow for high-impact reach and frequency management without the need for invasive user-level tracking.


What is the difference between a DSP and a cookieless DSP?Expand


Traditional DSPs rely on syncing third-party cookies across exchanges to build audience profiles, a process that is increasingly fragmented and unreliable. A cookieless DSP uses people-based identity, first-party data, and privacy-safe signals to reach consumers across all devices.


Viant DSP was purpose-built to be cookieless from the ground up, ensuring it never relied on the legacy infrastructure of third-party cookies.


What targeting options are available in a cookieless environment?Expand


Marketers in a cookieless environment can utilize a robust suite of options including contextual targeting, first-party data onboarding, and household-level identity resolution.


Furthermore, interoperability with alternative ID frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 allows brands to maintain significant scale across the open web. These diverse tactics provide a durable, privacy-forward alternative to outdated cookie-based audience segments.


How is campaign performance measured in a cookieless world?Expand


In a cookieless world, campaign measurement is achieved through modern attribution models such as[incrementality testing](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/incrementality-and-incrementality-testing-a-primer/) , Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), and secure data clean rooms.


The Household ID serves as a critical cross-device attribution layer, linking high-impact exposures on CTV to conversions on other digital devices within the home. This transition allows advertisers to prove ROI and optimize spend without relying on fragmented, cookie-based signals.
